doc.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

title: Memorable sessions: Patti LaBelle, Paul McCartney, the Meters
summary: Late-1960s to 80s sessions with saxophonist Alvin Thomas and trumpeter John Longo, including Patti LaBelle, McCartney's Venus and Mars, Neville Brothers and Meters; he played on Lady Marmalade.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Do you have any of the session work that you’ve done that sticks in your head as particularly memorable?

Oh quite a few of them man. The one that I did like from the late sixties up to the end of the seventies, even into the eighties. I had a friend of mine who was a saxophone player, he died in ’78 of lymphatic cancer. And we did a lot of sessions together in New Orleans. There was another trumpet player, his name was John Longo, who left New Orleans and went to play with the Ellington Orchestra. So it was John Alvin Thomas, the guy who died, myself, that we did a lot of sessions with people like Patti LaBelle and we did one

with Paul McCartney when he was in New Orleans, that album “Venus and Mars,” we did things like with the Neville brothers and a group with The Meters, which is a popular funk group. They’re still around but they’re not all together like they were, the original members you know. But back in the seventies man, they were one of the hot bands. We did a lot of like New Orleans type kind of grooves, “Hey Pocky A-Way” and things like that. So those are precious memories there, mainly because Alvin is gone and John is somewhere else. But I’ve done a lot with other musicians too that stick in my mind, but those sessions I did, they were like my brothers man, they were special.
I was poking around on the internet and for some reason I saw this thing about Lady Marmalade. You played on that?
Yeah I played on that with Pat LaBelle. I did two albums with her. Yeah. That was the one I was thinking about, yeah.
